item.title: Clearlake Todd Boehly: Are Chelsea Also-Rans Really Worth £5 Billion?
item.description: There are far less stressful ways to make a modest profit than dabbling in an English Premier League football club. But financier Todd Boehly must feel some relief to be leaving Chelsea FC without financial injury four years into a tough turnaround. He has handed US buyout firm Clearlake Capital full control — but control only counts for so much when you have limited freedom of movement.
item.dc:creator: Chris Hughes

item.title: The Fed Never Hikes Just Once? Alan Greenspan Disagreed
item.description: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Wednesday presided over the first US interest rate increase since 2023, and rate hikes are generally a package deal, as the aphorism goes. Versions of that folk wisdom circulated ahead of the decision, delivered by the likes of former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Jim Bullard and one-time Fed Vice Chair Richard Clarida. Their conviction is reflected in market pricing, with swaps traders anticipating around three more increases by late 202
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: Warsh’s Fed Soars Like a Hawk Into a Hiking Cycle
item.description: Unanimity reveals a resolve that wasn’t there before.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: The French Election Is Ignoring the Bond Market
item.description: The chief executive officer of insurance company AXA SA, Thomas Buberl, didn’t mince words Tuesday about the severity of France’s debt problem as global bond yields rise and the country’s risk premium over Germany hits its highest level in more than a decade. He called for reforms to get public finances under control and said a proposal by the far left to cancel debt held at the central bank was “dangerous” and “play(ing) with fire.”
item.dc:creator: Lionel Laurent

item.title: AI Boom: How to Stop Data Centers From Taking Too Much Electricity
item.description: The rapid expansion of data centers has become one of the most tangible expressions of the artificial intelligence revolution. But debate about their environmental, economic and social impact threatens their future development. And rightly so. Although the digital economy is often seen as weightless, every cloud service and AI application depends on massive physical infrastructure that takes up land, consumes energy, uses water and requires ever-increasing investment.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Sanchez

item.title: Laissez-Faire Hong Kong Meets the Five-Year Plan
item.description: Milton Friedman was baffled by Hong Kong. During his second visit in 1963, there was pulsating activity all around him — but no official data. Why wasn’t the colonial administration crowing about its achievements, he asked. The absence of a gross domestic product series wasn’t an oversight, as John Cowperthwaite, Hong Kong’s financial secretary at the time, explained to the celebrated American economist: “If I let them compute those statistics, they’ll want to use them for planning.”
item.dc:creator: Andy Mukherjee

item.title: The Supreme Court Has a Clear Logic on Election Interference
item.description: This week, four of the six conservative justices helped to block the Trump administration’s mail-in ballot scheme from going into place this Election Day. That’s a relief, but such partisan shenanigans aren’t permanently out of the question.
item.dc:creator: Noah Feldman

item.title: Why Gavin Newsom Is Willing to Wait for Kamala Harris
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom blew more than a few minds this week when he said that he wouldn’t mount a highly anticipated bid for president in 2028 if his longtime frenemy, former Vice President Kamala Harris, decides that she wants to run too.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: Mamdani's AI Ban in New York Schools Is Worth Copying
item.description: It used to be conservatives who wanted to tread carefully with new things. These days, it’s progressives sounding the alarm on artificial intelligence. And I’m not just talking about the risk of human extinction.
item.dc:creator: Abby McCloskey

item.title: Temporary Protected Status for Immigrants Needs Reform Not an End
item.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has temporarily deprived Democrats of a potent midterm rallying cry and averted a crisis for El Salvador’s president, one of President Donald Trump’s top fanboys, by tacitly agreeing to continue shielding 170,000 El Salvadorans from deportation — a protection that was set to expire on Sept. 9. DHS now says that a decision “will be made at the appropriate time,” in effect suspending the immigrants and their families in a fearful limbo.
item.dc:creator: James Gibney

item.title: California’s Electric Utilities Are Becoming Uninvestable
item.description: Climate change has lengthened California’s wildfire season by several months. The state’s wildfire politics season, meanwhile, has become perpetual. Sacramento just botched another opportunity to bring it to an orderly close, making a chaotic outcome for the state’s power grid and how the costs of wildfire damage are spread more likely.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: Trump's AI Cheerleading Is Becoming a Republican Liability
item.description: President Donald Trump just doesn’t get AI.
item.dc:creator: Nia-Malika Henderson

item.title: The US Can Slow Down AI and Stay Ahead of China
item.description: When Chinese leader Xi Jinping visits Washington next week, artificial intelligence will be near the top of the agenda. The dialogue that the US and China began earlier this year has gained urgency as fears of out-of-control AI have spurred calls for a slowdown in innovation at the frontier.
item.dc:creator: Hal Brands
